title: Contextual Cost Panel — motion-driven handoff & stakeholder QA
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design and handoff of a contextual cost panel that surfaces per-rollout token cost and realtime estimated spend using motion and microinteractions to indicate freshness and cached content. This ticket covers final visual polish, motion specs, dev-ready redlines, accessibility checks (contrast, keyboard nav), and a short stakeholder QA pass focused on edge-case collapse states and density modes.
background_and_goals: Users need a lightweight contextual cost surface embedded in the rollout inspector that communicates: current estimated spend, delta vs baseline, and whether values are live or cached. The goal is to reduce cognitive load while providing clear affordances to open the full cost drilldown. Motion should help indicate state transitions (live update, cached restore, error).
acceptance_criteria: Figma file linked in artifacts contains final frames for default / compact / collapsed / loading / error states
Motion keyframes exported and documented (duration, easing, delayed children, reduced-motion alternatives)
Handoff package includes redlines, token names, and a short dev checklist for implementing prefix caching indicator and live vs cached microcopy
QA checklist passed: keyboard focus order, screen reader label for cost delta, 3 contrast checks >= 4.5:1
Stakeholder (PM + Eng + Design) sign-off recorded in comments
tasks: Refine motion easing and durations (0–2000ms) and document reduced-motion behavior
Produce pixel-accurate redlines and export CSS token suggestions
Create small animation sprite for cached->live transition to avoid jank on low-powered devices
Coordinate with ENG for a canary implementation in console-frontend branch 'DES-91357-cost-panel'
Run a focused QA session with 3 product stakeholders and record findings
comments: 2026-03-10 — Asha K: Initial concept uploaded to Figma. Two density variants (default, compact) included. Noted potential performance concerns for animations on i3-equivalent environments.
2026-03-11 — Priya Shah (PM): Added success criteria for live vs cached labelling. Ask: include explicit tooltip copy for cached state explaining TTL and last-refresh time.
2026-03-12 — Omar Li (Engineering): Flagged that the KV cache indicator needs a backend flag; ENG-23412 created as dependency. Suggested a CSS-only micro-animation fallback.
2026-03-13 — Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Uploaded redlines and motion tokens. Implementer notes: will provide a prefetched SVG sprite and fallback opacity transition. Linking branch PR once ready.

2026-03-14 — Elena M. (Accessibility): Reviewed contrast ratios and suggested darker neutral for delta badges. Recommended aria-live politely for cost updates; avoid polite interruptions every second.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Motion will be subtle (scale + opacity + color fade) to avoid distracting users during multi-item rollouts
Fallback path: CSS-only transition when the browser can't run keyframe sprite; sprite used only on Chromium-based renderers for smoother frames
We will display 'cached' badge for estimates older than 45s; this threshold chosen as compromise between update noise and perceived freshness
Avoided embedding full cost drilldown in the inspector to keep surface lightweight — CTA opens full panel instead
qa_notes: Focus QA on collapsed->expand keyboard behavior (space/enter toggles), ensure focus returns to trigger after close
Test reduced-motion setting across macOS and Windows; animation should be removed and replaced with instant state changes
Simulate slow networks and confirm cached badge and tooltip appear within 2s of a failed realtime call
Edge-case: verify layout when token amounts are long (locales with separators) and when rollout name wraps to two lines
next_steps: Finish PR with .svg sprite and CSS tokens — targeted for ENG review by 2026-03-16
Schedule 30-minute stakeholder QA on 2026-03-17 (invite: PM, Eng lead, Accessibility)
After sign-off, create dev task to add server-side TTL flag and a test harness for cached vs live states
